Walk-in divider along z=6 (x -12..3.9167). TWO doors: (1) hall->walk-in at x1.4167 (36", hinge W, opens N), and (2) a NEW primary-bedroom->walk-in door near the EAST exterior wall (x-10, 32", hinge E, opens N into the closet) so the walk-in joins the primary suite.
EAST CENTRAL HALL south wall (z=-1, x -1.0833..3.9167): now SOLID. The primary-bedroom entry moved to the hall's EAST wall.

Primary <-> en-suite (extension) separator at x=-12. The door is near the NORTH-WEST corner of the bath (opening z 0.60..3.27, a 6 in return from the north face), hinged on its north jamb and opening east, so the leaf parks toward the north wall and the whole west wall south of it is the shower's.

WEST BATH south wall (z=-1, x 20.0833..31): SOLID. The SW bedroom no longer opens into the bath.

items._note: WEST BATH (x 20.0833..31, z -1..6). Shower on the NORTH wall (x 24..27.5), shallow 2.5 ft depth since the room is only ~7 ft N-S. Toilet in the west bay BETWEEN the west wall (x31) and the shower's west edge (x27.5), facing S with ~21 in clearance each side. Vanity in the SE corner (faces N). All clear of the entry-door swing.

ALCOVE toilet, a conventional tank, backed onto the WEST wall: the anchor sits 1.1 ft in front of the wall face (-12.229; buildToilet's tank runs -1.1..-0.6), centred in the alcove's 3 ft clear width (pz -3.688..-0.688), 18 in each side; the bowl's front (-14.229) leaves 2 ft to the open east end.

FREESTANDING TUB in the south-east corner, running NORTH-SOUTH and SQUARE to the walls (wFt is the E-W footprint, dFt the N-S), 28 in x 66 in. Its east side stands 12 in off the east wall's face (-22.688 -> -21.688) and its south end 6 in off the south wall's; the north end leaves 1 ft 7 in to the vanity and the walkway to the shower's arch is 25.5 in. The floor filler stands at the north end, the vanity side. DO NOT TILT IT. A tilt was asked for and tried at 15 degrees (measured: it widens the footprint from 2 ft 4 to 3 ft 8, and with only 5 ft 6 of room beside the shower it cut the walkway to 17.5 in) and then at 10 in BOTH directions, each shipped and each rejected on sight. The owner settled it square. At these clearances an angled tub reads as knocked askew rather than placed, because it stays nearly parallel to two walls it is inches from; the version that could work is a bigger angle with the tub pulled well off both walls, which costs the walkway.
FAMILY ROOM (landing north bay, x 3.9167..15.0833, z 5..16.0833): sofa against the west wall facing the TV on the east wall, with a rug between.
77-inch TV on the east wall facing W toward the sofa (screenFt = 5.6 ft wide, 16:9 -> ~3.15 ft tall -> 6.42 ft / 77 in diagonal), on a 6 ft media console.

PRIMARY EN-SUITE (extension x -22.92..-12, z -11.92..4), one open room. DOOR near the NW corner on the west wall. Double VANITY on the EAST wall centred on the north-east window (z -0.74), a sink and mirror either side of the glass, sconces outboard, counter at 34 in under the sill. Double SHOWER along the WEST wall, 8 x 5 ft, long side on the bedroom partition, two heads on that wall, a 6 ft SEGMENTAL arched doorless entry facing the room (springs at 6 ft 3, rises 1 ft 9 — a semicircle would apex above the ceiling). Five feet deep so that the west south transom (px -14.73) is CENTRED in its south end wall, equal tile either side, and is cut out of it (side cutout, da = (px_window - px_shower) * A[0] for a shower opening E). Wall-hung TOILET on the south wall near the SE corner under the east transom, facing north. No WC room. The ceiling over the shower rakes 8.47..8.89 (see level2 slopedCeiling), so the tile stops LEVEL at 8.4, just under its lowest point, with the raked plaster above — the usual detail; the tile does not rake. Its tiled walls are the PARTITION thickness (wallFt 0.4583): the north end wall continues as the water closet's east wall, one line from the south wall to the WC's north wall, and a 3.6 in tile wall meeting a 5.5 in partition read as one wall with a step in it. The two heads are on the back (west) wall at 7 ft 0 with a valve under each: the back-wall branch of buildShower used to hard-code them at 5 ft 6 and drew no valve at all.

TOILET ALCOVE, north side. A single full-height partition returning from the WEST wall (its face, px -12.229) at 90 degrees and running 4 ft east to px -16.229. With the shower's north wall (pz -3.688) as the other side, that makes an alcove 3 ft wide by 4 ft deep, OPEN to the east: the toilet is centred in it with 18 in each side and 2 ft of clear floor in front of the bowl. It replaces the enclosed water closet that stood here — two partitions and a pocket door — which the owner asked to open up. Full height under the shed ceiling, so topFt is z(px) at both ends; buildPartition draws a doorless raked wall as one trapezoid.

WATER CLOSET toilet, a conventional tank, on the WEST wall inside the WC north of the shower: the anchor sits 1.1 ft in front of the wall face (-12.229; buildToilet's tank runs -1.1..-0.6), centred in the 3 ft clear width (pz -3.688..-0.688), 15 in each side; the bowl's front (-14.229) leaves 2 ft 9 in to the WC's east wall face (-17.0).

En-suite lighting, kept simple: the vanity's own two sconces (`sconces: true` on the vanity item), two recessed over the shower (2.7 ft off its end walls), one in the WC over the toilet, two along the entry. Each of the two ground-room boxes this level reuses holds a fixture, so no generic ceiling light appears. Each can's ceilFt is the raked ceiling at its px: 8.0 + 0.0833 * (px + 22.9167).
The alcove's can, over the toilet. ceilFt is the raked ceiling at its px: 8.0 + 0.0833 * (px + 22.9167).
